focus: EmitterFrame orthonormality, vertical/coincident aim, roll convention, and source center; excludes photometry integration and scene-transform roll transport.

actual.method: GitHub fetch_file at the pinned commit; static source and test review only.

checks.evidence: EmitterFrame validates both Positions and finite roll in -180...180 before constructing target-source. UnitDirection rejects a zero vector, so coincident source and target return nil. Position bounds keep coordinate subtraction finite.

For horizontal magnitude > 1e-12, right normalizes (normal.z,0,-normal.x); up normalizes normal cross right. Algebra gives right cross up aligned with normal and pairwise orthogonality, subject to floating-point rounding.

Exact vertical aims choose right=(1,0,0), yielding up=(0,0,-1) for upward normal and up=(0,0,1) for downward normal. Near-vertical fallback can leave right dot normal bounded by 1e-12, below the assigned test's 1e-10 orthogonality tolerance; no material defect identified.

Rolled right=c*right+s*up and rolled up=-s*right+c*up preserve handedness and the normal. +90 maps right to up and up to -right; -90 reverses that rotation; +/-180 flips both plane axes. Exact cardinal coefficients avoid trigonometric residue, and zero roll preserves existing coordinates.

EmitterFrame direction uses target-source, StudioPhotometry.frame forwards light.position as source, and rectangular-emitter construction forwards light.position as center. No substitution of world origin or target for emitter center was found.
UnitDirection scales by the largest absolute component before calculating length, rejecting nonfinite/zero inputs and avoiding overflow or underflow from directly squaring raw components.

testFrameOrthonormalIncludingVertical checks generic, upward, downward, negative-Z and near-vertical targets; verifies pairwise dot products and handedness; and rejects coincidence. The assigned StudioOpticsTests file has no direct nonzero-roll or translated-source frame test. This is a scoped coverage observation, not a claim about other test files.
